title: Furniture Showroom Product Configurator
description: An interactive 3D product showroom where users configure a living room display featuring a luxury leather sofa and a designer helmet displayed as an art object on a pedestal beside it. Users adjust material finishes, lighting mood, camera angles, and generate a shareable product card with validated parameters.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive product showroom configurator. Load SheenWoodLeatherSofa.glb centered on the floor and DamagedHelmet.glb placed on a programmatically created cylindrical pedestal (radius 0.3, height 0.8, metallic gray material) positioned 1.5 units to the right of the sofa. Scale the helmet to roughly 0.6 so it reads as a decorative art piece. Set up a ground plane with a subtle reflective MeshStandardMaterial. Use a warm ambient light (intensity 0.4), one directional key light, and two movable RectAreaLights simulating studio softboxes. Camera starts at position (0, 1.5, 4) looking at the scene center. Add OrbitControls with damping enabled, constrained polar angle between 10 and 80 degrees, and min/max distance 2 to 8. Build an HTML overlay panel with these interactive controls: (1) A dropdown to select lighting mood from Warm Studio, Cool Gallery, or Dramatic Spot, each changing light colors and intensities with validated transitions. (2) A color picker that tints the sofa wood trim by traversing the sofa model and adjusting materials whose name contains wood. (3) A slider (0.0 to 1.0) controlling helmet metalness across all helmet meshes. (4) A button to toggle wireframe overlay on both models. (5) A Capture View button that reads current camera position, lighting mood, wood tint hex, metalness value, and wireframe state, validates all parameters are within expected ranges, and displays a formatted product card div overlay showing all values. (6) A Reset button restoring all defaults with smooth animated transitions using GSAP or manual lerp in the render loop. Validate that metalness is a float between 0 and 1, tint is a valid hex color, and mood is one of the three allowed strings before generating the card. Use requestAnimationFrame loop, enable tone mapping ACESFilmic, set renderer outputColorSpace to SRGBColorSpace, and add a subtle environment map using PMREMGenerator with a simple RoomEnvironment for realistic reflections on both models.
